results.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Reverse Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing towards you). Bend at your hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping them close to your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Breathe out as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and breathe in as you lower them back down.
Ensure your elbows remain close to your body throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
results.description: Dumbbell Bent-Over Reverse Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Bend at your hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping them close to your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Breathe out as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and breathe in as you lower them back down.
Ensure your elbows remain close to your body throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
results.description: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Goblet Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keep your knees slightly bent and your core engaged.
Push your hips back and hinge your torso forward while keeping the dumbbell close to your chest and your back straight.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor or until you feel a comfortable stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright position, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Push your hips backward instead of bending forward through your waist.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your lower back.
Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your feet and heels.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Goblet Good Morning is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Hammer Grip Incline Bench Two Arm Row
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Lie face down on the bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand using a hammer grip (palms facing each other).
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor, fully extended, with your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
results.description: Dumbbell Hammer Grip Incline Bench Two Arm Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie chest-first against it, allowing your arms to extend opposite your chest with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down.
Row both dumbbells backward by bending your elbows and pulling them towards your sides.
Return the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and avoid swinging.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Select a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row
instructions: Begin in a wide stance with one foot pointing forward and the other pointing to the side. Bend your knees, lean forward, brace your free hand on your thigh, and hold the dumbbell between your legs with an overhand grip.
Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your torso still, rotating your hand from an overhand grip to an underhand grip as your elbow moves upward and backward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your hips and shoulders steady.
Lower the dumbbell with control while rotating your hand back to an overhand grip, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso still without twisting as you lift the dumbbell.
Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Keep your working shoulder down and avoid shrugging as you row.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell upward and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Row (Rack Support)
instructions: Stand facing a dumbbell rack, placing your left hand on the rack for support. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip, arm extended down.
Lean downwards, step back with your right leg and keep it extended, bending both knees slightly and keep your back flat.
Pull the dumbbell upward towards your hip, bending your elbow and keeping it close to your body, focusing on squeezing your back muscles.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Avoid rotating your torso; keep your shoulders square to the floor.
Focus on using your back muscles to lift the weight, not your arm.
Breathe out as you pull the dumbbell up and breathe in as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Row (Rack Support) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip. Bend your knees and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging below your shoulders.
Brace your core and pull both dumbbells toward your abdomen by driving your elbows upward and backward close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your torso fixed.
Lower both dumbbells with control until your arms are fully extended and the dumbbells touch the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and your torso nearly parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbells toward your abdomen rather than toward your chest.
Keep your torso still and avoid using momentum to lift the weights.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells upward and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Pullover (Bent Arm)
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench, with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, following the same arc as you lowered it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
Ensure your back and shoulders are firmly supported on the bench.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far behind your head to prevent shoulder strain.
results.description: Dumbbell Pullover (Bent Arm) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Pullover on Floor
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Just before touching the floor, pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to protect your joints.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell back over your chest and inhale as you lower it.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
results.description: Dumbbell Pullover on Floor is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.
